1.45.betting_forecast: 15/8 Esna, 2/1 Sacred Ground, 4/1 Lilt, 9/1 Maldives, 12/1 Jennifer Jane, 16/1 Brigid's Well, 20/1 Spinning Lizzie.
1.45.spotlight_verdict: The Gosden stable is usually the first place to turn for a winner of this race and their Sacred Ground was runner-up in a Listed race here on her second start. Brian Meehan's Esna, however, has much better form thanks to her fourth in the Group 1 Marcel Boussac, a performance which gave encouragement for 1m2f even though she's by the sprinter Starman. One who might just scupper them both is LILT, who is one of two William Haggas-trained entries for the 1m Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot and one of his three in the Irish Oaks. With class in her pedigree too, it may be worth taking the chance that she can take the leap forward that's required to make this a winning reappearance.[Richard Austen]

horses.spotlight_comment: Made all in one 1m novice as a 2yo and very nearly did so in another; 11-1 fourth of ten in Listed race here (1m, good to soft; Sacred Ground was second) on final start illustrated some limitations, sticking to her task well as if this longer trip would suit but, despite the Oaks entry, she probably has serious work to do in this company too.

All three starts as 2yo were on soft; green in front in 7f novice win at Sandown against a notable rival; about 2l fourth of eight when an outsider for 1m Group 1 Marcel Boussac at Longchamp, keeping on well while never able to threaten seriously the lead; fair chance she'll stay 1m2f, judged on that, even if pedigree (sire sprinter) casts doubts on her Oaks entry; clear top on form.

Made all in a maiden at Wetherby (7f, good to firm) on second start and almost all in Listed race at Sandown (7f, good) later last summer; her season ended, however, with last of seven in Group 3 at Goodwood (7f, good to firm) in August; good chance she will stay 1m2f; needs to resume progress.

Lope De Vega half-sister to winners Doom (7f/1m including Listed; RPR 104) and Kilt (1m; 97); dam a well-related 1m-1m2f winner (including US Grade 1; 116); 7-2 for a six-runner maiden at Doncaster (7f, soft) in October, dictating a steady pace and battling on well to win by a neck; that's just fair form but this 1m Coronation Stakes and 1m4f Irish Oaks entry looks the type to do a lot better as 3yo.

2,900,000gns yearling by Camelot; first foal of Group-placed 7f 2yo winner (RPR 102), herself a half-sister to multiple Group 1 winner Luxembourg; 8-1 in steadily run novice at Yarmouth (1m2f, good) three weeks ago, short of room for a sustained period before running on into second of seven; Irish Oaks entry who is bottom on ratings but probably capable of a lot better.

By Kingman out of Oaks winner Anapurna; favourite for both starts as 2yo, overcoming greenness to win a five-runner novice at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) and every chance through the final 3f when second of ten in Listed race at Newmarket (1m, good to soft); Oaks entry from a stable which has a fine record in this race and houses the current Oaks favourite, so market strength would probably be telling.

Insole Rossa Ryan 20-1 96 79 105 Won debut as 2yo but twice came up short in Group events; resumed with a late charge to grab a conditions stakes at Kempton (1m, AW) in March but the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good; 22-1, made most) proved too tough and, despite a new trip, the same is likely to be the case today.

2.20.betting_forecast: 4/1 Cathedral, Survie, 9/2 Falakeyah, 7/1 Sand Gazelle, 9/1 Chantilly Lace, 11/1 Stateira, 12/1 Francophone, 14/1 Jancis, 16/1
2.20.spotlight_verdict: Another chance is given to FALAKEYAH whose highly promising first couple of starts featured a powerful performance on this card last year. She may fulfil her potential this term and has been found the ideal starting point. Sand Gazelle, who has broadly progressive form, is second choice. Cathedral and Survie have a combined record of only 1-17 since October 2024 but they are respected on ratings.[Steve Boow]

horses.spotlight_comment: Steady progress culminated in close second to Cheshire Dancer in Group 3 at Ascot (1m) on King George day last year; not in the same form since and this is a stiff task even if she rebounds.

Ran well off top weight in handicap at the Newmarket Craven meeting (1m, good) but has something to find on ratings off level weights in this higher grade; not disgraced in Goodwood Listed event on Saturday.
horses.breeding: ch m Harry Angel - Magic Nymph

horses.spotlight_comment: Possibly unsuited by soft ground; record of 0-8 since debut success doesn't do her justice, with three good efforts at Group/Grade 1 level (1m/1m3f) among her form; leading player on ratings returned to turf with AW reappearance under her belt.
horses.breeding: b f Too Darn Hot - War And Peace

horses.spotlight_comment: Lightly raced; good fifth in the 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes prior to close third in Ascot Group 3 won by Cheshire Dancer; below par in final 3yo start but consistent otherwise and may rebound.
horses.breeding: b f Lope De Vega - Seeking Solace

horses.spotlight_comment: Developed into a very useful sort last term, notably Group/Grade 3 performances at Ascot (won) and Kentucky Downs (ran well); chance of landing this prize depends on the effects of first-time headgear.
horses.breeding: gr m Phoenix Of Spain - Kristal Xenia

horses.spotlight_comment: Has proved headstrong and she was disappointing in last two appearances, including when only 5-2 for the Coronation Stakes having bypassed the Oaks and French Oaks, but this may be the time to catch her; comfortably justified favouritism in the Pretty Polly on this card (good to firm) 12 months ago, taking record to 2-2 and looking a potentially high-class filly; worth another chance.
Form for the Gosdens featured a Listed win last August and close second in Newmarket Group 3 in October (both 1m2f); sold for 750,000gns since; this is harder but she may do better still.

Low-mileage filly; below form at Newmarket when last seen but broadly progressive otherwise and may have more to offer this term; Listed winner at York (1m2f) last July then ran well in Group 3 at the Curragh (1m1f); shortlisted.

Ex-French mare who has several pieces of Group 1 form over middle distances, including a Saudi effort since joining new yard this year; unsuited by drop back to 1m last time when one place behind Cathedral, losing her unbeaten AW record; big player on peak figures.

2.55.betting_forecast: 9/2 Dramatic Star, 5/1 Subsequent, 6/1 Align The Stars, Many Men, 7/1 Goblet Of Fire, 8/1 Bahadur, 10/1 Kihavah, Pole Star,
2.55.spotlight_verdict: There has been so much to like about topweight Subsequent but most of it has been delivered on good to soft or soft ground. He has big-race entries and still needs plenty of respect but it might be best to turn elsewhere if the rain has not arrived in significant quantity. Align The Stars (second choice) began the season in revitalised fashion with his win at Kempton, while Many Men kept on improving last term, but a review of this race last year will show that KIHAVAH, the old man of the party, could also have a major chance. He was luckless that day and, although tilts at big prizes in Dubai this year did not see him to best effect, last August's Ebor showed that plenty of ability remained.[Richard Austen]

horses.spotlight_comment: Thereabouts on occasions in 2025, crept down the weights and broke his losing run in clearcut style when he reappeared five weeks ago wearing restored cheekpieces in the Queen's Prize at Kempton (2m, AW); back up 4lb but showed plenty of bottle in that win and may have turned a corner.
horses.breeding: br g Sea The Stars - Kitcara

horses.spotlight_comment: Industrious and dependable sort over 1m6f-2m2f, who's fit from AW, but his turf strike-rate is just 1-17 and that makes him look vulnerable.

Made immediate progress when switched to AW in the autumn, completing a hat-trick in a 1m4f novice and 1m4f/1m6f handicaps; perhaps in need of the race (albeit joint-favourite) on reappearance four weeks ago, but now needs to show that he can serve up his best on turf.

Moving up to 1m4f worked well in December and comparable form at 1m6f/2m since, including another win three starts back; he's come up a bit short in warmer races this year, though, including behind Align The Stars at Kempton, and none of his turf form (admittedly at up to 1m2f) is close to this mark.
horses.breeding: b g Dark Angel - Venturous Spirit

horses.spotlight_comment: Had underwhelming hurdle and AW campaigns before his second of five when returned to Flat turf at Beverley (2m) 18 days ago; this demands markedly better and his 2024 and 2025 turf records aren't that persuasive.
horses.breeding: b g War Command - Storming Sioux

horses.spotlight_comment: Improved last year without quite winning; each-way claims if back to best with first-time headgear after two rather disappointing runs in 2026.
horses.breeding: b g Sea The Stars - Dramatic Queen

horses.spotlight_comment: All of his Flat success for this yard has been on AW, albeit with good-ground hurdle wins too and he was runner-up at Goodwood (1m6f, good to firm) last August; has a run under his belt this term but to win this would require a new best performance on turf.
horses.breeding: b g Saxon Warrior - War No More

horses.spotlight_comment: Saw daylight all too late when strong-finishing fifth in this race last year (much better than his 2024 performance in it); Meydan this January/February did not yield much (stiff tasks) but he's now 4lb lower than this time last year, too well handicapped to be ruled out; rare run in cheekpieces.

Excellent progress last term included three handicap wins (1m2f, 1m6f and 2m) in March-July and an agonisingly close call in the Melrose at York in August; close fourth in 1m6f Listed race at Ascot on final outing; well below that form on 2026 reappearance but that may have put him right.
horses.breeding: b g Study Of Man - Mariee

horses.spotlight_comment: Won two 1m6f handicaps last term and two respectable efforts in valuable races in late summer; just 10-1 for 2m2f Cesarewitch at Newmarket on final 3yo outing, which did not work out, and he was just 15-8 when fading into fourth of six at Newbury (2m) 16 days ago on first run since he was gelded; connections now turn to a visor and drop him back in trip.

Excellent 3yo season culminated in his Listed win at Ascot (1m6f, soft) and, after a delayed reappearance last year, he found career-best form to win a good handicap at Doncaster (14.5f, good to soft; tongue tied second time) in September on final outing; the Yorkshire Cup and Ascot Gold Cup entries are striking but ideally he would be on ground softer than good.

Started 2025 with a bang for new connections when winning a slowly run, four-runner Group 3 at Ascot (2m, good to firm) in April; remote with ambitious targets on next three starts and although sixth of 11 in 2m handicap at Chester in September was an upturn, markedly better is required to win this..

3.35.betting_forecast: 9/4 Precise, 9/2 Venetian Sun, 13/2 True Love, 8/1 My Highness, 10/1 The Prettiest Star, 14/1 Abashiri, Evolutionist, 16/1
3.35.spotlight_verdict: The Karl Burke-trained VENETIAN SUN (nap) is taken to reverse Moyglare placings with Precise, who nevertheless commands major respect despite a slight interruption in her training this spring. The selection brings the significant achievement of beating colts in the Morny to complete a notable summer hat-trick and, having prepped nicely with a racecourse gallop last month, there's a good chance that her progress will resume. My Highness (second pick) and Domina Ignis (third choice) are interesting, with striking resemblances to the 2014 and 2024 winners of this prize, while True Love helps to give Ballydoyle a strong hand. Several others have possibilities, as one would expect in a big-field Classic.[Steve Boow]

horses.spotlight_comment: Well-bred filly, by Frankel out of a 1m2f Group 1 scorer for her connections; quickened smartly and recorded an impressive 4l success in Kempton maiden (1m, AW) six months ago; the shortest on experience, being the sole once-raced contender, but brings major potential; interesting.

Belied her 50-1 odds with neck success in the Nell Gwyn (upped to 7f, good; Group 3) on seasonal debut, taking strike-rate to 3-8 and form figures on the Newmarket tracks to 121; doesn't look a budding star and only two fillies in the last 40 years have landed that trial then followed up in the 1,000 Guineas; may well come up short.

From the family of Enable; edged ahead close home in C&D handicap (good; ran off a mark of 83) at the Craven meeting, adding to her 2yo AW wins; it's hard to knock an improving filly who remains unbeaten (3-3) but her form is a long way short of Classic standard, as BHA ratings reflect.
horses.breeding: b f Too Darn Hot - Contribution

horses.spotlight_comment: Very similar profile to the 2024 Guineas winner Elmalka, having won at Southwell in sole 2yo start then finished third in the Fred Darling (Group 3); gained her success (6f, AW) in emphatic fashion despite taking a good hold, then was beaten only 2l with hood fitted at Newbury (7f, good) despite being hampered; bred to stay 1m and looks open to further progress.

Newmarket form comprises a maiden win on the July course and third-place finish, just over 4l behind Precise, in the Group 1 Fillies' Mile; bagged Group 3 honours at Longchamp (1m, good) on reappearance, collaring a sitting duck (clear leader who tired) and strong at the finish; has evidently trained on well and her RPRs continue on an upward trajectory.
horses.breeding: ch f Night Of Thunder - Model Guest

horses.spotlight_comment: Ended her 2yo campaign with quite a tidy success in Group 2 at Deauville (7f, good) to complete a hat-trick; beaten favourite (finished second, splitting outsiders) in the Prix Imprudence over the same C&D on reappearance but that was also the case with the same yard's Miss France, who rebounded to land this prize in 2014; likely to be suited by stepping up to 1m; enters calculations, with a resumption of improvement plausible.

Frankel filly who has been campaigned exclusively over 7f at Newmarket, producing good performances (won maiden and second in Group 3) from the front last autumn and then not asked to lead when only sixth, beaten favourite, in the Nell Gwyn; may still have more to offer but this is a difficult task in terms of form and tactical considerations.

Ended her 2yo campaign with quite a tidy success in Group 2 at Deauville (7f, good) to complete a hat-trick; beaten favourite (finished second, splitting outsiders) in the Prix Imprudence over the same C&D on reappearance but that was also the case with the same yard's Miss France, who rebounded to land this prize in 2014; likely to be suited by stepping up to 1m; enters calculations, with a resumption of improvement plausible.

Has something to find at this level but is open to further improvement and would be particularly interesting if the ground is on the soft side, having shown her 2yo promise on slower than good, namely a narrow success in newcomers' event at Deauville (7f) and a rallying fourth in the May Hill at Doncaster (1m Group 2).

Scored with something to spare at Southwell (AW) in sole 2yo start, then did well to finish sixth in the Fred Darling at Newbury (again over 7f) having been slowly away, met traffic issues and been forced to switch; remains a nice prospect for Tom Clover but this assignment demands another big leap forward on bare figures.

Proved a useful sprinter last season, notably winning over 5f at Glorious Goodwood in the summer and over 6f at Newmarket (beat Azleet in good-ground Listed contest) final outing; not an obvious 1,000 Guineas player, with doubts over the new trip and the deeper waters (she's a stone below the standard required).

Daughter of her connections' July Cup winner Starman; duly showed plenty of promise in both 2yo starts, recording a clearcut success at Nottingham (6f, good) and close second, clear of remainder, in the Rockfel at Newmarket (7f, good to firm; Group 2); gives the impression she'll be suited by this further step up in distance; possibilities with additional improvement on the cards.

Held on gamely in 1m Listed event at Newcastle on seasonal debut, taking AW record to 2-2 and overall strike-rate to 4-6; may win more races at the right level but looks out of her depth in this company returned to turf, as her two defeats (both Group 2) attest.

In the same ball park as stablemate Precise on ratings and, like that filly, is a Group 1 winner at Newmarket (Cheveley Park Stakes over 6f); landed the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot (5f) earlier in her 2yo campaign and added a Group 3 prize, with something to spare, at Leopardstown (7f, good to yielding) on reappearance; has a solid record aside from an excusable defeat at the Breeders' Cup; upped further in trip and has stamina on the dam's side; one of the main players.
horses.breeding: b f No Nay Never - Alluringly

horses.spotlight_comment: Career commenced with two wins, the second one on the Newmarket July course; record of 0-5 since reflects that her limitations are rather exposed, and this is a markedly stronger Guineas than the Jumeirah 1,000 Guineas in which she went close at Meydan (1m, good; Listed) last time.
horses.breeding: gr f Time Test - True To Herself

horses.spotlight_comment: Belied market position (rank outsider) by finishing second to Precise in the Group 1 Fillies' Mile over C&D but needs to prove she can back up that apparent improvement; may be flattered by her new rating and, combined with a record of 0-5 since debut success, doesn't look a solid contestant.

Absent since finishing third to Precise in the Moyglare Stud Stakes when upped to 7f at the Curragh, losing her unbeaten record but far from disgraced and sticking on in a manner that suggests she'll stay 1m this year; 4-4 previously and completed a notable 6f hat-trick with wins in Group 3 at Royal Ascot, Group 2 at Newmarket (July) and Group 1 at Deauville; may well rate higher still and add to an already impressive tally; pleased her trainer in a racecourse gallop last month; highly respected.

4.10.betting_forecast: 5/2 Call Me Tomorrow, 11/4 Crownbreaker, 3/1 Efsixteen, 8/1 Lazurite, 10/1 Havana Sprite, 12/1 Donna Beauty, 16/1 Pageant
4.10.spotlight_verdict: Pageant Girl has already put her head in front but she faces a stiff task conceding weight to some interesting opposition. The market can help sort out the newcomers, of which Crownbreaker (second choice), Efsixteen and Lazurite appeal most, but CALL ME TOMORROW shaped well here at the Craven meeting and can put her experience to good use.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: Weak 9-1 shot for her C&D debut 18 days ago but she made a bold bid, travelling strongly but finding one too strong in the closing stages; that effort was backed up by the Topspeed figure and she sets a useful standard for the newcomers to aim at before factoring in progress.

March foal; 550,000gns yearling; fourth foal; Minzaal half-sister to winners Mill Stream (6f including 2yo/Group 1 July Cup; RPR 120) and Asymmetric (5f/6f including 2yo Group 2; 109); dam 5f/6f winner (including 2yo; 83); strong paper claims for a trainer who is already off the mark with his 2yos.

March foal; 35,000gns yearling; seventh foal; Starspangledbanner half-sister to four winners including Grocer Jack (1m2f/10.5f including German/Italian Group 3; RPR 116) and Ghislaine (7f-8.7f including Listed; 99); dam German 1m-1m3f winner (including Group 3; 104); not obviously precocious on paper but worth a market check.

Late April foal by Havana Grey; 135,000gns yearling, 350,000gns breeze-up 2yo; eighth foal; sister to 5f/6f winner Pilgrim (including 2yo; RPR 106), half-sister to winners Moraawed (6f/7f; 92) and Crash Helmet (6f AW; 71); dam 5f 2yo winner (74), half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Temple Meads; looks the part on paper and she makes her debut with her yard in form.

January foal; 150,000gns yearling; second foal; Havana Grey half-sister to 5f 2yo winner Polly Darling (RPR 71); dam 6f/6.5f 2yo winner (93); stable 0-2 with their 2yos this year but had one run well behind Call Me Tomorrow last month.

April foal by Bungle Inthejungle; 17,000euros yearling; sixth foal; sister to 5f/6f winner Lily In The Jungle (including 2yo; RPR 74), half-sister to 5f 2yo winner Lili Wen Fach (69); dam 5f winner (71), out of half-sister to 5f 2yo Group 3 winner Show Me The Money; bred to have a future but she is starting out in a potentially hot contest.

March foal by Blue Point; £175,000 yearling; closely related to 6f-1m winner Hallasan (including 2yo; RPR 99), half-sister to four winners including Al Raya (5f 2yo including Group 3; 105), Grisons (5f-6f; 79) and Mystify Me (5f; 70); dam 5f and 6f (Listed) 2yo winner (99); trainer has had a winning 2yo newcomer this year; William Buick booked.

Promise amid inexperience on her Beverley debut (5f, good to soft) and still looked a work in progress when winning a 6f novice at Ripon eight days ago; had the benefit of the rail to help her but she kept on well enough; she will need to progress again to defy a penalty against some interesting opposition, though.

4.45.betting_forecast: 11/4 Jaan Ki Tukri, 3/1 Napa, 11/2 Agamemnon, Persian Spring, The Dancing Pirate, 10/1 Beauty For Love, Noble Raider.
4.45.spotlight_verdict: Agamemnon and Persian Spring are newcomers of note but JAAN KI TURKI and Napa both shaped well at Newbury. Clive Cox's juvenile can confirm the placings and get off the mark at the second attempt.[Paul Smith]

horses.spotlight_comment: February foal by Mehmas; £72,000 yearling, 150,000gns breeze-up 2yo; first foal of a once-raced 7f 2yo winner (RPR 89); trainer off the mark with 2yos this year; William Buick booked; market confidence would look significant.

March foal by Blue Point; 140,000euros foal, 130,000euros yearling; sixth foal; closely related to Italian 7.5f-1m2f winner Conquering Eagle, half-brother to winners Apricot Ice (6f; RPR 95), Saraqael (1m; 93) and Seasony (7f/1m including 2yo/AW/Czechia; 79); dam Group-placed 1m winner (100); enough paper appeal to warrant a second look.

Promise amid inexperience when third of nine in a 5f maiden (good ground) at Newbury 16 days ago, racing freely early on and paying the price in the closing stages; finished a neck in front of Napa on that occasion and can confirm the placings.

Sent off favourite for his Newbury debut 16 days ago (5f, good) and ran creditably, not helped by being a bit tight for room inside the final furlong; finished a neck behind Jaan Ki Tukri on that occasion and he is no banker to reverse the placings.

Always on the back foot on his Wolverhampton debut 12 days ago (5f) and although he ran on for second, he was no threat to the easy winner; should have learned from that initial experience but connections look to hold stronger claims with Napa.

April foal; 100,000gns yearling by Persian Force; eighth foal; closely related to 6f 2yo winner Beauty Inspire (including Group 3; RPR 102), half-brother to winners Darwell Lion (7f-8.6f including 2yo/AW; 97) and Camera Shy (6f/7f including 2yo/AW; 78); dam French 1m4f winner, out of 5f/6f winner; represents a powerful yard; shortlisted.

May 28 foal by Blackbeard; third foal of a smart 6f/7f winner (including Group 3; RPR 106), herself from an excellent family; should have a future but comfortably the youngest of these and he will need to be useful to make a winning start.

5.20.betting_forecast: 7/4 Study Of Words, 7/2 Crockham Heath, Sahara King, 11/2 Evanesco, Gatehouse.
5.20.spotlight_verdict: Charlie Appleby's STUDY OF WORDS was runner-up to a promising sort (who has big-race entries) on his second start, before breezing clear from negligible opposition over C&D on his final 2yo outing. The form of that win is hard to pin down but he may have been let in lightly even off today's opening mark of 95. Crockham Heath and Gatehouse are on hat-tricks following their AW exploits but the selection may have most to fear from Sahara King who made eye-catching late headway in a strong 1m2f conditions stakes 16 days ago.[Richard Austen]

horses.spotlight_comment: Well beaten at 50-1 on debut here (7f, good) in October; way better, however, for front-running wins in a Southwell novice (1m) in November and seven-runner handicap at Wolverhampton (9.4f) in January; those wins were AW but with authority last time (8lb higher today) and he could be a useful prospect.
horses.breeding: b c Sea The Moon - Ultramarine

horses.spotlight_comment: Pretty useful in two of his five efforts as 2yo; second favourite for handicap/seasonal debut over C&D (good) 18 days ago but weakened in the final 1f into fourth of eight; that was creditable but he needs to build on it.
horses.breeding: b c Too Darn Hot - Golden Gazelle

horses.spotlight_comment: All three runs were on AW, with plenty of promise on debut before he won a novice at Chelmsford (1m2f) in December and seven-runner handicap by a short head at Southwell (1m) in April; return to 1m2f should suit and, although he's been raised 4lb, further improvement is possible.
horses.breeding: b g Ten Sovereigns - Wild Intrigue

horses.spotlight_comment: 16-1 for novice at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in November but always prominent and led final strides; 14-1 in a hot novice at Newbury (1m2f, good) 16 days ago and made late gains to finish on heels of the leaders in a blanket finish; set for further improvement and likely to prove better than this opening mark at some point soon.
horses.breeding: b c Too Darn Hot - Kahala Queen

horses.spotlight_comment: Marked improvement through three-race 2yo career, beating a fair maiden by 15l when he won a four-runner maiden at 1-7 over C&D (good) final start; that can't be the most solid form but he could hardly have done it more easily and is a Derby entry; fascinating handicap debutant in first-time headgear.
